title: A pilgrimage
hook: a journey to a place that matters: the dying Buddha named four, and the psalms sang on the road up to Jerusalem
tomorrow: a storm was filling the boat, and Jesus slept. how could he?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: away. The rains retreat stops the travel and stays in one place. Today, the other kind of going: a journey with somewhere to arrive.

People cross oceans to stand outside the house where a singer grew up, or to walk the street in an old photo of a grandparent. Nothing is there to take home. They go anyway. The Buddha's attendant, Ananda, understood the pull. His teacher was dying, and Ananda had a worry. Monks used to come from everywhere to see him. When he's gone, where will they go?
screen: `THE HOUSE WHERE A SINGER GREW UP.` → `NOTHING TO TAKE HOME.` → `ANANDA'S WORRY.` → `WHERE WILL THEY GO?`

segments.voice: Lying between two trees at Kusinara, the Buddha answered with four places. Where the Tathagata was born. Where he woke up. Where he first set the teaching rolling. And where he passed away. A faithful person, he said, should visit them with reverence. Buddhists still make that journey: to Lumbini, his birthplace, to Bodh Gaya, where a Bodhi tree still grows on the spot, to Sarnath, where he first taught, and to Kusinara itself. That's the teaching inside his answer. The teacher would be gone, but the ground where it happened would still be there to stand on, and standing there stirs a person. Here's a neighbor who knows that road. In the Hebrew Bible, a group of psalms carry the title song of ascents, and tradition says pilgrims sang them going up to Jerusalem. One begins: "I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the LORD." The same gladness, the same feet on the road, going to the place where something happened. And one honest difference. The Torah sets the times: "Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the LORD thy God in the place which he shall choose." Going up is a commandment, tied to the festivals, and the psalm sings it glad. The Buddha set no festival and no date. He named four places worth the journey, to be visited with reverence, whenever a person goes.
screen: `ANANDA: WHERE WILL THEY GO?` · `FOUR PLACES TO VISIT WITH REVERENCE.` · `I WAS GLAD WHEN THEY SAID UNTO ME.` · `FIXED FESTIVALS, OR ANY TIME.` · then, large: `THE JOURNEY.`

segments.voice: Choose a place that matters on your own path: where someone you love was born, where something in you changed. Say its name once, under your breath. For the rest of the sit, picture the last stretch of road before you'd arrive.
A pilgrimage: a journey to a place where something happened, like the Buddha's four places, or the road the psalms went up.
Your line: the journey. The Buddha offered four places, and the psalm went up glad. Day 1644, and the year's holy days are gathered in.

howItsDone: Buddhist pilgrims visit Lumbini, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath and Kusinara, the four places the Buddha named. Jewish pilgrims once went up to Jerusalem at the festivals, and tradition says they sang the Psalms of Ascent; some people also make personal journeys to family places.
